opex.note: Building the app, recommendation systems and new formats like video podcasts and audiobooks — down 3% YoY as personnel costs fell with the timing of annual equity grants shifting to Q2.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning listeners and advertisers — down 3% YoY on lower marketing spend and personnel costs.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — up 1% YoY.

follow100Note: Of every $100 of revenue, $90 came from Premium and $10 from ads. Direct costs took $68.35 and running costs $19.50, a net finance loss took $4.32 and tax $2.46, leaving $5.37 kept as profit. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Spotify reports in euros under IFRS. Dollar figures are converted at €1 = $1.0815 (ECB euro reference rate at Mar 31, 2025 — the Q1 release states no rate, unlike Q2). As reported: revenue €4,190M · gross profit €1,326M · operating income €509M · net income €225M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago (+15% constant currency)

oneTimers: Operating expenses included €76M of 'social charges' — Swedish payroll taxes on share-based pay that swing with Spotify's share price; €75M of it was tied to share-based compensation, versus €82M a year ago, and the charges came in €58M above forecast as the share price rose.

Finance costs included a €180M paper loss on the Exchangeable Notes — the notes are worth more when Spotify's share price rises, which books as a cost, and it reverses if the share price falls. A year ago the same line was a €35M loss.

The quarter carried a €103M income tax expense on €328M of pre-tax income — a 31.3% effective tax rate, versus a €23M tax benefit a year ago. The rate was driven mainly by €47M of tax on the non-deductible Exchangeable Notes loss, partly offset by a €22M deferred tax benefit and an €8M benefit from income earned in lower-tax jurisdictions.
otherDetail: Finance items netted −$196M — a €180M paper loss on the Exchangeable Notes as Spotify's share price rose, plus €58M of foreign-exchange losses, €8M of lease interest and €6M of other costs, partly offset by €65M of interest earned on Spotify's cash pile, €2M of lease interest income and €4M of other finance income.

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Subscriptions — 268 million people paying monthly, up 12% YoY; revenue per user (ARPU) €4.73, up 4% as price rises outweighed product mix; gross margin 33.5%.

segments.name: Ad-Supported
segments.note: The free tier's advertising business — revenue grew 8% (5% in constant currency) across music and podcasting; its gross margin jumped to 15.3% as podcast and music costs improved.

sources.label: Official Q1 2025 shareholder letter (SEC EDGAR 6-K Exhibit 99.1)

takeaways.text: Premium subscribers grew 12% to 268 million and monthly active users rose 10% to 678 million — 5 million new paying subscribers in the quarter, 3 million above Spotify's guidance. Premium revenue grew 16% to €3,771M on subscriber gains and price rises.
takeaways.title: Subscribers keep compounding

takeaways.text: Gross margin rose to 31.6%, a Q1 high and up 403 bps YoY. Premium gross margin reached 33.5% on audiobooks and music, and Ad-Supported gross margin jumped to 15.3% on better podcast and music contribution. Operating income more than tripled to a record €509M, a 12.1% margin.
takeaways.title: Margins widened again

takeaways.text: Operating income of €509M was cut by finance costs of €252M — mostly a €180M paper loss on the Exchangeable Notes as Spotify's share price climbed, plus €58M of foreign-exchange losses — and a €103M tax bill, leaving net income of €225M, up 14% YoY. Cash told a stronger story: free cash flow hit a record Q1 €534M, up 158%.
takeaways.title: Paper losses shrank the bottom line

verdict: Spotify grew revenue 15% to €4.19B (about $4.5B) and added 5 million paying subscribers, with operating income more than tripling to a record €509M — but a €180M paper loss on its Exchangeable Notes and a €103M tax bill held net income to €225M.
